topics.label: Introduction to cancer biology and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the core learning outcomes, and frames cancer as a disease of cellular differentiation.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe cancer development through accumulated genetic alterations that disrupt normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the benign-to-malignant transition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on mechanisms of local invasion, metastatic dissemination, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Principles of tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard naming conventions and major exceptions used to classify benign and malignant neoplasms by tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the local and systemic pathophysiological mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Patterns of cancer incidence across humans and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the incidence and mortality of different tumor types in human populations and across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical applications of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the clinical rationale, methodology, and varying efficacy of population screening programs for detecting pre-malignant and malignant lesions.

topics.label: Conclusion and upcoming practicals preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and providing closing housekeeping remarks.
